rationale_summary: Broad indices near highs with 88% of assets positive over 21 sessions, but leadership is rotating hard: precious metals, EM and biotech leading while defense, industrials, utilities and regional banks sold off. Macro is soft-growth/sticky-inflation (payrolls -23k, core CPI 2.5%, PCE 3.3% core y/y) with the Fed on hold and a hawkish minority; 10y fell to 4.63%. Big in-window catalysts: Nvidia earnings, Jackson Hole, Sept 4 payrolls, Sept 11 CPI, Sept 15-16 FOMC. Dispersion is high, so a small number of high-quality relative pullbacks offers the cleanest reversal setups.
portfolio_rationale: In a high-dispersion, mixed-pattern tape, the best risk-adjusted setups are high-quality relative pullbacks with shallow drawdowns and positive prior trends: industrials, regional banks and small-cap value all show deep recent active declines against solid prior relative strength, low-to-moderate volatility, and no briefing evidence of fundamental deterioration. Falling long yields and broadening breadth (RSP beating SPY over 5 sessions) support the domestic cyclical/value reversal. Persistent losers with negative trend in both windows (defense, utilities, solar, oil) and high-beta momentum extremes (crypto, semis into Nvidia) are excluded from the top ranks.
key_risks: Nvidia results on Aug 26 could drive a broad index move that swamps sector reversal edges; Sept 4 payrolls and Sept 11 CPI plus the Sept 15-16 FOMC could shift rates sharply against cyclicals and regional banks; Consumer softening (confidence 89.4, retail sales -0.6%, home sales -10.5%) could extend weakness in domestic cyclicals and small caps; Reversal candidates' pullbacks may reflect early fundamental deterioration not captured in the frozen briefing; Continued momentum in gold, metals and crypto could keep leadership away from value/cyclicals for the whole window
